subject: ss-infectious-diseases
title: Antimicrobial stewardship: core principles for exam and practice

steps.tx: **Antimicrobial stewardship** is a coordinated set of actions that makes sure each antibiotic prescription is the right drug, dose, route and duration for the patient. Inappropriate prescribing is common, and surveys in acute care hospitals suggest that a substantial fraction of courses are unnecessary or suboptimal. Stewardship is one of three pillars of integrated healthcare strengthening, alongside **infection prevention and control** and patient safety.

steps.tx: The **Five D's**framework guides every prescription: right drug, right dose, right route, right duration and **timely de-escalation**. De-escalation means narrowing or stopping empirical therapy once culture and susceptibility results are known. A formal **antibiotic time out**, usually at about 48 hours, is the key moment to review cultures and decide whether broad coverage is still needed.

steps.tx: Procalcitonin guided discontinuation uses a blood marker of bacterial infection to decide when to stop antibiotics. When levels fall and the patient is clinically improving, the course can often be ended early. **Short course therapy** is also supported for many infections, such as community acquired pneumonia, where shorter regimens achieve similar cure rates. An **IV to oral switch** is appropriate once the patient is stable, absorbs enteral drugs and has no barrier to oral intake.

steps.tx: Stewardship is more effective when education is paired with **specific interventions** and **outcome measurements**, rather than teaching alone. Prospective audit and feedback, where a team reviews live prescriptions and reports back to the prescriber, is a core intervention. **Preauthorization** for restricted agents, especially broad-spectrum drugs, adds a check before the drug is dispensed. A **cumulative antibiogram** summarises local resistance patterns and guides empirical choices.

steps.tx: Stewardship outcomes matter because resistance and side effects carry real costs. Around one in five hospitalised patients on antibiotics has an associated adverse effect, and resistant healthcare infections can lengthen stays by roughly 6 to 13 days. Stewardship programmes are linked to lower **Clostridioides difficile** incidence. Laboratory **antimicrobial susceptibility testing** guides the individual regimen, so results must be quality checked before reporting.
